subject: QA gate playbook: acceptance criteria & canary policy clarifications
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sasha Greene <sasha@kitapp.com>
Date: 2028-11-02T09:12:00Z
Subject: QA gate playbook: acceptance criteria & canary policy clarifications

Hi team —

Quick context: KitApp is ready to run an A/B canary for the new prompt bundle (attached) and wants clear acceptance criteria so their PMs can greenlight a rollout. I pulled a first-pass checklist and a canary policy draft (canary_policy_v2.pdf attached). I need product and QA alignment on these questions before we share with KitApp ops:

- Proposed mandatory thresholds for a successful canary (suggested):
  • P95 latency <= 350ms (hosted).
  • Delta on our semantic accuracy metric (internal QA_score) <= -0.5% relative to baseline.
  • Hallucination incidents (as measured by promptset hallucination tests) <= 1 per 10k responses.
  • No critical safety signals in top-1000 monitored queries.

- Rollback triggers: immediate rollback for any security_compliance issue or >2% degradation on revenue-critical intent; automated throttling and manual rollback for other regressions.
- Sample sizing: what's the minimum sample size we require for A/B to be considered valid for KitApp's traffic?

Attachments: promptsuite_prompts_v3.jsonl (the prompt set), canary_policy_v2.pdf (policy + rollback flow), qa_metrics_snapshot.csv (latest staging metrics).

Questions for product/QA: are these thresholds reasonable? should we add any additional checks specific to KitApp (billing flows, cold-start intents)? Is the sample size suggestion below acceptable?

Proposed next steps:
- Product + QA to confirm thresholds and sample size by EOD Thu (2028-11-02).
- If agreed, we share the canary_policy_v2 + prompt bundle with KitApp and schedule a 1-hour kickoff (Ops + KitApp) next week.

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Product Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Sasha Greene <sasha@kitapp.com>
Date: 2028-11-02T11:07:00Z
Subject: Re: QA gate playbook: acceptance criteria & canary policy clarifications

On Thu, Nov 2, 2028 at 09:12 AM Jordan Blake wrote:
> Quick context: KitApp is ready to run an A/B canary for the new prompt bundle (attached)...

Thanks Jordan — I skimmed the attachments. A couple quick thoughts:

- The latency P95 looks fine for hosted; add a separate P95 cap for Private (if they choose Private deployment) — e.g., 500ms.
- The hallucination threshold is OK but we should define what counts as an "incident" (user-facing hallucination vs. internal labeling). I'll add a short definition to the policy.
- Sample size: for KitApp's traffic mix, I recommend at least 10k impressions per variant or a 7-day window (whichever comes first) to capture weekday/weekend variance.
- We should include a small manual-review checklist: 200 random samples evaluated by QA for false positives on billing intents.

Happy to jump on a 30-min alignment call tomorrow.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior PM, Safeguards & Evals
From: Sasha Greene <sasha@kitapp.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: KitApp Product Ops <ops@kitapp.com>, Eric Tang <eric.tang@vendorsec.com>
Date: 2028-11-03T08:03:00Z
Subject: Re: QA gate playbook: acceptance criteria & canary policy clarifications

Thanks Jordan and Marissa — KitApp can work with the proposed thresholds. A few clarifications from our side:

- We will run on Hosted for the canary. Private is not planned yet.
- We need the prompt bundle and a short readme for our PMs that explains what the hallucination metric means and how you compute QA_score. Can you share a 1-page summary?
- Timeline: KitApp can start the canary on Mon Nov 6 if we have the final acceptance checklist by EOD Fri (2028-11-03).

Eric (cc) from VendorSec is tracking the compliance artifacts; he asked for the canary_policy_v2.pdf and the sampling plan (we've attached vendorsec_request.pdf in a separate thread).

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
—Sasha
Sasha Greene
Head of Product Ops, KitApp
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sasha Greene <sasha@kitapp.com>, Eric Tang <eric.tang@vendorsec.com>
Date: 2028-11-04T15:50:00Z
Subject: Re: QA gate playbook: acceptance criteria & canary policy clarifications

Team — quick decision from leadership so KitApp doesn't miss their window:

- Approve the thresholds Marissa suggested (hosted P95 350ms; private P95 500ms fallback).
- Add the additional acceptance rule: relative degradation on revenue-critical intents must be < 0.5% (absolute) — anything above 0.5% blocks rollout and requires a hotfix/rollback.
- Minimum sample: 10k impressions per variant OR 7 full days; also require the 200-manual QA checks on billing intents.
- For any safety or compliance signal flagged by VendorSec, the canary must be paused within 30 minutes and a joint incident call scheduled.

Marissa: please update canary_policy_v2.pdf with the definitions and the manual-review checklist. Jordan: ensure the 1-page readme for KitApp that Sasha requested is created and shared.

I'll be copied on the kickoff email; if anything changes on timing, escalate to me.

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Head of Product — Platform
